metaDescription: Permacon and Allan Block interlocking retaining walls in Woodstock, Ontario, built for local soil with full drainage. Free written quotes, permits handled.
h1: Block Retaining Walls in Woodstock, Ontario
intro: Woodstock's mix of sandy and clay soil means the same block product can perform very differently from one yard to the next. We adjust the base and drainage design to the soil we actually find on site.

blocks.text: Garden terraces, sloped rear yards, and driveway edges are the most common places we build block walls in Woodstock and the surrounding Oxford County area. Block gives homeowners a finished, landscaped look without the cost of poured concrete.
On lots with sandy soil, extra care goes into base compaction so the wall doesn't settle unevenly over its first few years.

items: Permacon for a wide range of colours and finishes
Allan Block for larger or taller walls needing extra structural capacity
Unilock and Oaks as alternatives for a specific aesthetic
Can be curved to follow property contours
Freeze-thaw resistant with proper drainage behind the wall
Ontario Building Code compliant with correct engineering

sections.heading: Permits Through the City of Woodstock

blocks.text: Any wall over about one metre needs a City of Woodstock permit under the Ontario Building Code. We manage that process, including engineering for taller walls or ones near a driveway load.

sections.heading: Block Wall Lifespan in Oxford County

blocks.text: A properly drained interlocking block wall in the Woodstock area typically performs well for several decades. The main factor that shortens lifespan locally is drainage stone becoming clogged with fine sandy soil over time if filter fabric wasn't installed correctly.
See /how-long-do-retaining-walls-last for a material-by-material comparison, and /retaining-wall-maintenance-tips for what upkeep actually looks like.
Permacon and Unilock both offer sample boards showing available colours and textures. We can bring samples to the site visit so you can see how a product looks against your home before committing.

faqs.q: Which block brand do you recommend for a Woodstock backyard?
faqs.a: For most residential backyard walls, Permacon offers a good balance of appearance and cost. For taller or load-bearing walls, we typically step up to Allan Block.

faqs.q: Does sandy soil around Woodstock affect block wall installation?
faqs.a: It affects base preparation. We compact deeper and use a wider drainage stone bed on sandy sections to keep the base stable.

faqs.q: How much does a block wall cost in Woodstock?
faqs.a: Generally $200 to $350 per linear foot installed, depending on height and the block product chosen.

faqs.q: Can a block wall be built around an existing garden or tree?
faqs.a: Often yes. We plan the wall line around mature landscaping where possible, though root systems sometimes require adjustments to the design.

faqs.q: How often should a block wall be inspected?
faqs.a: A quick visual check once or twice a year, especially after heavy rain, is enough to catch early drainage issues before they become structural ones.

faqs.q: Can I see physical samples before choosing a block product?
faqs.a: Yes, we bring sample boards to the site visit so you can compare colours and textures in natural light against your home.

faqs.q: What happens if a block wall settles unevenly after installation?
faqs.a: Minor settling in the first year is normal as backfill compacts naturally under seasonal moisture changes. If a section settles noticeably more than the rest, we'll come back and assess whether it's cosmetic or points to a drainage or base issue that needs correcting.
